/-!
# Erdős Problem 65

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/65](https://www.erdosproblems.com/65)
- [GKS84] Gyárfás, A., Komlós, J. and Szemerédi, E., On the distribution of cycle lengths in graphs.
  J. Graph Theory (1984), 441-462.
- [LiMo20] Liu, H. and Montgomery, R., A solution to Erdős and Hajnal's odd cycle problem.
  arXiv:2010.15802 (2020).
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos65

/--
Let $G$ be a graph with $n$ vertices and $kn$ edges, and $a_1<a_2<\cdots$ be the lengths of
cycles in $G$. Assume $n>0$ and $k>0$. Is it true that
$$\sum\frac{1}{a_i}\gg \log k?$$

Gyárfás, Komlós, and Szemerédi [GKS84] have proved that this sum is $\gg \log k$, so that only
the second question remains.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_65.parts.i : answer(True) ↔
    ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ (k : ℝ) (hk : 0 < k),
      ∀ (n : ℕ) (V : Type) [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V),
        0 < n →
        Fintype.card V = n →
        (G.edgeSet.ncard : ℝ) = k * n →
        (∑ᶠ a ∈ G.cycleLengths, (1 : ℝ) / a) ≥ c * Real.log k := by
  sorry

/--
Is the sum $\sum\frac{1}{a_i}$ minimised when $G$ is a complete bipartite graph?

This problem is #65 in Extremal Graph Theory in the graphs problem collection.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_65.parts.ii : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (k : ℝ) (hk : 0 < k),
      ∀ (n : ℕ) (V : Type) [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V),
        0 < n →
        Fintype.card V = n →
        (G.edgeSet.ncard : ℝ) = k * n →
        ∀ (A B : Type) [Fintype A] [Fintype B],
          Fintype.card (A ⊕ B) = n →
          ((completeBipartiteGraph A B).edgeSet.ncard : ℝ) = k * n →
          (∑ᶠ a ∈ (completeBipartiteGraph A B).cycleLengths, (1 : ℝ) / a) ≤
            (∑ᶠ a ∈ G.cycleLengths, (1 : ℝ) / a) := by
  sorry

-- TODO: Add variants of the problem.

end Erdos65

findings.description: The statement is tagged `answer(True)` / `research solved` and asserts one uniform bound: ∃ c > 0 such that for ALL real k > 0, all n > 0 and every graph G with n vertices and exactly kn edges, ∑_{a ∈ C(G)} 1/a ≥ c·log k. The source's "≫ log k", as GKS solved it, is asymptotic in k: it holds for density k ≥ b with b a constant. For k ≤ 1 the Lean claim is vacuous (log k ≤ 0; proved in scratch). But for 1 < k < b it asks for more than GKS proved. Near k = 1 it is exactly the open sparse-regime problem. I proved in Lean that the right-hand side implies ∃ c > 0 such that for all 0 < ε ≤ 1, every graph with n > 0 vertices and (1+ε)n edges has ∑ 1/a ≥ c·ε/2, i.e. f(1+ε) ≥ cε/2 for Erdős–Hajnal's f(α) = inf{L(G) : |E| ≥ α|V|}. GKS explicitly leave this regime open. Gyárfás–Prömel–Szemerédi–Voigt only get f(1+1/k) ≥ (300 k log k)^{-1}, against an upper bound 77/(72(k+1)), so the needed bound f(1+1/k) ≥ c/k is not known and could be false. The formal statement is therefore strictly stronger than the claim the source poses and records as solved (the original implies the large-k version, checked in Lean). Its truth is open, so `answer(True)` is not justified by the cited result. The docstring's added "Assume n>0 and k>0" is where the range slipped.
findings.source_evidence: erdosproblems.com/65 (live page via reader proxy, 2026-09-23; LaTeX source): "Is it true that \sum 1/a_i \gg \log k? ... Gyárfás, Komlós, and Szemerédi [GKS84] have proved that this sum is \gg \log k, so that only the second question remains." GKS84 (J. Graph Theory 8 (1984) 441–462, intro): "It was conjectured by Erdős and Hajnal that f(a) ≥ c1 log(a) ... In this paper we prove that f(a) ≥ a log(a) if a ≥ b, for suitable constants a and b (Theorem 4'). The behavior of f(a) for a ∈ (1, 1+ε) seems to be an interesting problem." Theorem 4': "If G is a graph of density α, where α ≥ b, then L(G) ≥ a log(α)." GPSV (Combinatorica 5 (1985) 41–52): "Erdős and Hajnal introduced the real function f(α)=inf{L(G) : |E(G)|/|V(G)| ≥ α}. They asked about the behaviour of f(α) as α tends to infinity ... GKS showed that f(α) ≥ a·log α, provided that α > b ... The problem of determining the behaviour of f(α) for α ∈ (1,1+ε) has been raised in [GKS]. It was not even clear whether f(1+ε) > 0". They prove f(1+1/k) ≥ (300k log k)^{-1} for large k, and (Theorem 2) f((k+1)/k) ≤ 77/(72(k+1)). Liu–Montgomery (arXiv:2010.15802) likewise describe GKS as Σ 1/ℓ = Ω_d(log d), an asymptotic statement.
findings.suggested_fix:
Restrict to sufficiently large k, matching GKS Theorem 4', e.g.
`theorem erdos_65.parts.i : answer(True) ↔ ∃ c > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ k in Filter.atTop, ∀ (n : ℕ) (V : Type) [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V), 0 < n → Fintype.card V = n → (G.edgeSet.ncard : ℝ) = k * n → (∑ᶠ a ∈ G.cycleLengths, (1 : ℝ) / a) ≥ c * Real.log k`
This compiles, and the current statement implies it. Alternatively use `∃ k₀, ∀ k ≥ k₀`. Change the docstring to say "for all sufficiently large k". Optionally add a separate `research open` variant for the sparse regime (is f(1+ε) ≫ ε?), citing GPSV.

reformulations.difference: The source asks "Is the sum minimised when G is a complete bipartite graph?". The Lean fixes a real k > 0 and n > 0. For every G on n vertices with exactly kn edges, and every complete bipartite K_{A,B} with |A|+|B| = n and exactly kn edges, it requires s(K_{A,B}) ≤ s(G). There is no explicit n ≥ 2k condition, it uses 'exactly' rather than 'at least', and k is the real ratio |E|/n rather than the side size.
reformulations.equivalence_argument:
This is exactly Erdős's precise 1981 conjecture (Combinatorica 1 (1981), inequality (2): "Let n ≥ 2k then for every G(n; k(n−k)), Σ 1/a_i ≥ ½(½+⅓+⋯+1/k). In other words Σ 1/a_i is minimum for the complete bipartite graph of k white and n−k black vertices"). MMPS (arXiv:2609.26401) restate it as Conjecture 1.1: for 1 ≤ k ≤ n/2, K_{k,n−k} minimises s among n-vertex graphs with ≥ k(n−k) edges.
(Conjecture ⇒ Lean) Given A, B with |A|+|B| = n and |A||B| = kn > 0, let a = min(|A|,|B|), so 1 ≤ a ≤ n/2. K_{A,B} ≅ K_{a,n−a}, so the cycle lengths agree, and G has a(n−a) edges. The conjecture gives s(G) ≥ s(K_{A,B}).
(Lean ⇒ Conjecture) Given G with ≥ a(n−a) edges, delete edges to get G' ≤ G with exactly a(n−a) edges. Then C(G') ⊆ C(G), and all terms are positive with finite supports, so s(G') ≤ s(G). Apply the Lean statement with k = a(n−a)/n, A = Fin a, B = Fin (n−a).
Checked in Lean: the edge count of `completeBipartiteGraph A B` is |A|·|B| (from `encard_edgeSet_completeBipartiteGraph`), and the hypotheses are satisfiable non-trivially (K_{3,4}, n = 7, k = 12/7).

review.notes:
Lean experiments are in /workspace/review/scratch*.lean:
- (a) The range k ≤ 1 of parts.i is trivial.
- (b) The right-hand side of parts.i implies the sparse-regime bound f(1+ε) ≥ cε/2 for 0 < ε ≤ 1.
- (c) The suggested `∀ᶠ k in atTop` fix compiles, and the current statement implies it.
- (d) The edge count of `completeBipartiteGraph A B` is |A|·|B|, and the hypotheses of parts.ii are satisfiable.

`#check` shows parts.ii as `True ↔ …` only because `answer(sorry)` in `Prop` elaborates to `True` under the default `google.answer := alwaysTrue` setting. This is not a defect.

On parts.i: with integer k, or real k ≥ any fixed k₀ > 1, the statement follows from GKS (large k) plus GPSV positivity and monotonicity of f. Only k → 1⁺ is problematic. There GPSV's bounds, (300 k log k)^{-1} ≤ f(1+1/k) ≤ 77/(72(k+1)), leave the order open. Subdivided K_{2,t} gives about 1/(2k) from above. I found no later result settling it: Semantic Scholar lists only 4 papers citing GPSV, and none improves it. So parts.i as written is at best an open problem, possibly false.

On parts.ii: the file's `research open` matches the source. erdosproblems.com/65 still shows OPEN on 2026-09-23. Montgomery–Milojević–Pokrovskiy–Sudakov (arXiv:2609.26401, 22 Sep 2026) prove Erdős's 1981 conjecture only for sufficiently large k; the forum notes that small k is still open. The all-k statement in parts.ii therefore remains open. Maintainers may want to add a solved variant for large k (Er81 form, with k the side size, `∀ᶠ k in atTop`), and to watch whether erdosproblems reclassifies #65.

Two minor observations that do not affect the Lean: the erdosproblems remark says \"maximised\" where it means \"minimised\", and the module docstring does not cite Er81, the precise source of part (ii).

not_demonstrated.reason: The statement as formalized is open, not trivially true or false. Its content beyond GKS's large-k theorem is the sparse-regime bound f(1+ε) ≥ cε near k = 1. GKS 1984 call this 'an interesting problem'; Gyárfás–Prömel–Szemerédi–Voigt 1985 prove only f(1+1/k) ≥ (300 k log k)^{-1}, with an upper bound 77/(72(k+1)), and I found no later result closing the gap. A proof would need GKS plus this open result. A disproof would need a family of sparse graphs beating c·ε, which is not known. Nothing about the statement over the reals is decidable in small cases. I proved in scratch that parts.i implies the sparse-regime bound, but that shows only that the statement is stronger than the solved claim, not that it is provable or false.

submission.summary: I bailed out, and no trivial-proof file was created. The misformalization I reported in Erdos65.erdos_65.parts.i is a quantifier-range slip: it says "for all k > 0" where the solved result (GKS Theorem 4') covers only density k ≥ b. That slip turns the problem, which the file tags solved with answer(True), into one that is open, possibly false, in the sparse regime k → 1⁺. Because the formal statement's truth is unknown either way, it has no short honest proof or disproof. The supporting Lean facts from the review are in the scratch files, not in a trivial-proof file. Part (i) restricted to k ≤ 1 is trivial. Part (i) implies f(1+ε) ≥ cε/2 for 0 < ε ≤ 1. The suggested `∀ᶠ k in atTop` fix compiles, and the current statement implies it.
submission.gave_up_reason: My only finding, Erdos65.erdos_65.parts.i, has no short proof or disproof, because the truth of the formal statement is unknown either way. It asks for ∑ 1/a ≥ c·log k for ALL real k > 0, uniformly in c. Proving it needs the full Gyárfás–Komlós–Szemerédi theorem for large k (real mathematics). It also needs the sparse-regime bound f(1+ε) ≥ cε as k → 1⁺, which GKS left open and Gyárfás–Prömel–Szemerédi–Voigt only got to ε/(300 log(1/ε)). Refuting it needs graphs of density 1+ε with ∑ 1/a = o(ε), i.e. lim inf f(1+ε)/ε = 0; that is also open, since the known upper bound is only O(1/k). There is no counterexample to compute and no unsatisfiable hypothesis. The one formal fact I have, in scratch2.lean, is that parts.i implies the sparse-regime bound. That neither proves nor refutes the statement, so I did not present it as a demonstration. I never created /workspace/review/trivial_proof.lean, so there was nothing to delete.
